title: Air-fryer paneer
subtitle: Spiced paneer cubes air-fried until golden and crisp at the edges.
excerpt: Paneer cubes marinated in yoghurt and spices, then air-fried until the edges are golden and slightly crisped while the inside stays firm and squeaky. Ready in 15 minutes. Serves two as a side.
sourceNotes: Paneer is a fresh Indian cheese made by curdling milk with an acid. It does not melt when heated, which makes it suitable for frying and grilling. Air-fried paneer is used as a component in North Indian dishes including paneer tikka and palak paneer.

recipe.makeAheadNotes: Marinate for up to 4 hours in the fridge for deeper flavour.

content.text: Paneer cubes develop a golden, slightly crisp exterior in the air fryer when the marinade contains yoghurt ,  the sugars in the yoghurt help the surface colour without needing oil. A 30-minute marinade is enough; longer gives a deeper flavour. Soak the paneer in warm water for 5 minutes before marinating if it has been stored in brine, which removes the excess salt.

Mix {{plain-yoghurt}} of yoghurt with {{cumin-ground}} of cumin, {{garam-masala}} of garam masala, {{turmeric}} of turmeric, {{chilli-powder}} of chilli powder, {{garlic}} of grated garlic, and {{sea-salt-fine}} of salt. Add the {{paneer}} cubes and stir to coat. Leave for at least 30 minutes.

Preheat the air fryer to 200°C. Spray the basket with cooking oil. Shake excess marinade off the paneer cubes and place in a single layer. Cook for 6 minutes, turn, and cook for a further 5-6 minutes until golden and slightly charred at the edges. Serve immediately.

items.symptom: Paneer sticking and tearing when turned
items.cause: Moved too soon or basket not oiled.
items.fix: Spray the basket before cooking and wait the full 6 minutes. Once the marinade crust has set, the cube releases cleanly.

items.cause: Marinade too thick or excess not removed.
items.fix: Shake off the excess marinade before cooking. A thick coat of wet yoghurt steams rather than charring.

items.cause: Overcooked or paneer dried out before marinating.
items.fix: 12 minutes total is the maximum. If your paneer is old or has dried out, soak in warm water for 5 minutes before marinating.

content.text: Air-fried paneer cubes work as a component in a wrap with sliced onion and mint chutney, or as a side with a dal and rice. Toss them into a warm spinach curry in the last few minutes, or serve simply with naan and a salad of sliced tomato and onion.
